summary: A 300 mm foundry line in Shenzhen's Pingshan District run by SMIC's Shenzhen subsidiary. Under a March 2021 framework agreement with the Shenzhen government, SMIC planned USD 2.35 billion of new investment for about 40,000 wafers a month on 28nm and older processes, aimed at display-driver and power-management chips. SMIC reported that the line entered production by the end of 2022.

location.note: The fab is in Pingshan District, according to a 2021 district project notice reported by trade press.

metrics.note: Estimated new investment, subject to a definitive agreement.

milestones.note: Cooperation framework agreement with the Shenzhen government disclosed.
Production start expected at the time of the 2021 agreement.
SMIC said the fab entered production by the end of 2022; Jiemian later called Runpeng's line the second 300 mm line to start production in Shenzhen, after SMIC's.

notes: The operating status rests on SMIC's report that the line entered production by the end of 2022; SMIC's later results releases no longer report progress by fab, and no newer dated source read for this record confirms production on this line, so the status is unconfirmed since February 2023. Jiemian's undated report on the Runpeng line, which started on 31 December 2024, still called SMIC's the first 300 mm line producing in Shenzhen. SMIC's 2025 annual results and first-half 2026 report list SMIC Shenzhen among the subsidiaries on the mandatory environmental disclosure list, and the first-half 2026 report carries a Shenzhen plant expansion project at 98% of its budget without saying which line it covers.
